idiom_name: durable instance record + (state, event) -> next-command decider + deadline sweep + compensation mapping
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep one durable record per process instance keyed by the business correlation identifier, holding the current state, the data collected so far, the pending requests and their deadlines, and a version marker for the process definition. The decider is a pure function from (state, event) to the next state plus zero or more outgoing commands; it never performs I/O itself, so it can be tested exhaustively. Commit the state transition and the outgoing command atomically (outbox or transactional channel), then let a sweeper or timer service fire expired deadlines; unmatched or malformed replies go to a dead letter channel instead of being dropped. Every command handler must be idempotent, and every irreversible step needs a compensation that is itself idempotent and safe to run twice.
code_sketch:
on_message(msg):
    p = load(msg.correlation_id)                 # durable instance record
    if msg.id in p.handled: return               # idempotence by message id
    next_state, commands = decide(p.state, msg)  # pure decider
    begin()
      save(p, next_state, msg.id)
      for c in commands: outbox.enqueue(c)       # same transaction
    commit()
    for c in commands: send(c)

every tick: for p in due_deadlines(): decide(p, Timeout)
pitfalls: Keeping instance state in memory or in a single global variable instead of one durable record per correlation identifier.
Deciding and sending outside the state transaction, which duplicates or drops steps after a crash.
No deadline handling, so instances whose reply never arrives stay pending forever.
Treating the participants as transactional: they are at-least-once and must be idempotent.

Wrong move: default to a central process manager for every cross-service interaction -> the coordinator can become a bottleneck and single point of failure -> instead use choreography for simple, loosely coupled event flows and reserve orchestration for complex branching or visibility needs.
